headline: Lawmakers On Verge of Deal to Ban Chinese Cars, Moreno Says
author: Steven T. Dennis

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- US lawmakers are closing in on an agreement to shut China's fast-growing automakers out of the US market that avoids entangling Mercedes-Benz Group AG, Senator Bernie Moreno said.

The Ohio Republican spearheading the effort said in an interview Friday that all major issues have been resolved, including changes to protect the German automaker, which is about 20% owned by Chinese entities.
"We're super, super, super close," Moreno told Bloomberg at the Capitol. "All the big issues are resolved."

If enacted, the measure would wall off the world's second-largest auto market from China's automakers such as BYD Co., which have rapidly grown around the world with technology-packed electric vehicles that often undercut Western competition on price. Although tariffs and technology restrictions already effectively block Chinese cars from the US, enshrining a ban into law would go a step further.
Bloomberg reported Thursday that lawmakers were nearing an agreement to ban Chinese cars.

Carmakers in the US have urged Congress to adopt the ban, citing economic and national security threats posed by subsidized Chinese cars equipped with software and hardware that can transmit data about American drivers and infrastructure.

Moreno said negotiators are still working out some technical details about the legislation. The goal is to ensure the same bill can pass both the House of Representatives and the Senate, either on its own or packaged with another bill like the annual defense policy legislation.
Earlier legislation under consideration would have prohibited sales of connected vehicles by automakers that are more than 15% owned by Chinese entities.

That risked jeopardizing Mercedes' business in the US. The German carmaker is nearly 10% owned by China's BAIC Motor Corp., a state-owned carmaker. Li Shu Fu, the billionaire founder of Chinese carmaker Geely, also holds nearly 10% of Mercedes' shares, putting the company above the earlier bill's 15% threshold.

"The Mercedes issue is not even on the table anymore," Moreno said. "The bill is about banning Chinese predatory vehicles that affect national security, economic security. Mercedes doesn't affect either one of those."
Moreno also said there is agreement on language regarding battery technology.
"We're down to the final technical details, and hopefully we'll get it across the finish line when we get back," he said.
